o.text:
From Old Anatolian Turkish کیجه (gejä), Proto-Turkic *kēče (“night, evening, yesterday”). Cognite with
Turkish gece (“night”),
Turkmen gije,
Crimean Tatar gece,
Tatar кичә (kiçä, “yesterday”),
Uyghur كەچە (keche),
Kazakh кеш (keš, “evening”),
Kyrgyz кеш (keş, “evening, late”).
From Proto-Turkic *bẹńŕ (“swelling; scar, ulcer”) cognate with Turkish bez, пӳр (pür, “pus”), etc.

glosses: to stop (to cease moving or to not continue)
to stand for a while while waiting for something
to hold on, to wait a short while (especially in the imperative mood)
to linger, to stay somewhere for too long, to be delayed
to have fun, to have a good time, to amuse oneself

o.text: Calque of Russian контро́льно-пропускно́й пу́нкт (kontrólʹno-propusknój púnkt).

Izafet II compound of buz + dağ. Calque of English iceberg.

* Uzbek muztogʻ,
* Kazakh мұзтау (muztaw),
